title: Ultrastructural localization of de novo synthesized phosphatidylcholine in yeast cells by freeze-fracture electron microscopy
protocol: Inoculate yeast cells on an agar plate in 2 mL of SD + CA + ATU medium in a culture tube.
Grow at 30°C while shaking at 200 rpm for 12–16 h.
Measure optical density at 600 nm (OD600) using a spectrophotometer.
Dilute the yeast culture with 10 mL of SD + CA + ATU medium to an OD600 of 0.001 in a glass conical flask.
Grow yeast cells until they reach an appropriate density.
Transfer 3 mL of the yeast culture to a new culture tube.
Add 3 μL of 1 M propargylcholine to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM.
Culture yeast for an additional 30 min at 30°C while shaking at 200 rpm.
Collect cells by centrifugation at 1,500 × g for 1 min and discard the supernatant carefully.
Suspend cells in 4% formaldehyde in 0.1 M sodium phosphate buffer by pipetting and incubate for 15 min at RT with gentle agitation.
Collect cells by centrifugation at 1,500 × g for 1 min and rinse them once with an ample volume of PBS.
Resuspend cells in 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS and incubate for 10 min with gentle agitation (e.g., 50 rpm) on a shaker or rotator.
Collect cells by centrifugation at 1,500 × g for 1 min.
Rinse cells twice with an ample volume of 0.1 M Tris-HCl (pH 7.5) by centrifugation at 1,500 × g for 1 min.
Mix 1 μL of 1 M CuSO4, 10 μL of 10 mM TBTA in DMSO, and 5 μL of 0.5 M ascorbic acid in DW in a 1.5 mL microtube.
Leave the solution for 10 min at RT.
Add 983 μL of 0.1 M Tris-HCl (pH 7.5) to the tube.
Add 1 μL of 0.5 mM AFDye546 picolyl-azide to the tube and mix well.
Add the click reaction solution to pelleted cells, suspend them by pipetting, and incubate for 20 min at RT.
Collect cells by centrifugation at 1,500 × g for 1 min.
Rinse cells three times with an ample volume of 0.1 M Tris-HCl (pH 7.5).
Put the cell pellet between the glass slide and the coverslip using an appropriate mounting medium.
Observe under a fluorescence microscope (Excitation 554 nm/Emission 570 nm).
Perform quick-freezing and prepare freeze-fracture replicas as described in Fujita et al. (2010) and Tsuji et al. (2019).
Incubate replicas in PBS containing 20 μg/mL Zymolyase, 0.1% Triton X-100, 1 mM dithiothreitol, and 1% BSA for 2 h at 37°C.
Incubate replicas in 0.1 M Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) containing 2.5% SDS at 60°C for 12–16 h.
Rinse the freeze-fracture replicas three times with 0.001% Triton X-100 in 0.1 M Tris-HCl (pH 7.5).
Treat replicas with 2% cold fish gelatin and 0.001% Triton X-100 in 0.1 M Tris-HCl (pH 7.5) for 10 min at RT.
Mix 1 μL of 1 M CuSO4, 10 μL of 10 mM TBTA, and 5 μL of 0.5 M ascorbic acid in a 1.5 mL microtube.
Leave the solution for 10 min at RT.
Add 983 μL of 2% cold fish gelatin in 0.1 M Tris-HCl (pH 7.5) and 0.5 μL of 10 mM biotin-azide to the tube.
Mix well to prepare the click reaction solution.
Critical: Click reaction solution must be prepared immediately before use.
Incubate replicas in click reaction solution for 30 min at RT.
Rinse replicas five times with 0.001% Triton X-100 in 0.1 M Tris-HCl (pH 7.5).
Rinse replicas once with PBST.
Incubate replicas with 2% cold fish gelatin in PBS for 30 min at RT.
Rinse replicas with PBS once.
Centrifuge diluted mouse anti-biotin antibody solution at 21,000 × g at 4°C for 5 min and use the supernatant.
Incubate replicas with mouse anti-biotin antibody (5–10 μg/mL) in PBS containing 1% cold fish gelatin for 12–16 h at 4°C.
Rinse replicas five times with PBST.
Centrifuge GAM12 diluted solution at 200 × g at 4°C for 5 min and use the supernatant.
Incubate replicas with goat anti-mouse antibody conjugated with 12 nm colloidal gold (GAM12) in PBS containing 1% BSA for 30 min at 37°C.
Rinse the replicas five times with 0.1% BSA in PBS.
Rinse the replicas twice with distilled water.
Pick up the replicas on Formvar-coated EM grids (50 mesh, copper).
Dry the replicas on filter paper.
Take photos randomly by transmission electron microscope.
Measure the area of membranes using ImageJ.
Count the number of colloidal gold labels.
Calculate the density of gold labels for each area.
Compare the results statistically using the Mann-Whitney U test or other appropriate methods.
